reason: The local recount holds: old LDA zp(3)+PHA(3)+PLX(4)+STX zp(3)=13 cycles, 6 bytes; new LDX/STX/LDX/STX zp = 12 cycles, 8 bytes. All opcodes are plain 6502 and the 65SC12 has them. list_b (&6E) and list_n (&53) are both zero page, no other name sits at &6E, and the only reads of list_b are in each_b, which sets it first. X, flags and A on exit are the same. So the change is correct and saves 1 cycle an execution (1.9 executions a pass measured: 5.706/3 at &98EE). It is 2 bytes bigger, not 2 smaller. What I refute is the page-crossing account. The +2 shift runs past render_end (&A366) through bank 4's tables and the straight sprites to &B3xx: no ALIGN or gap soaks it up. The claim checked branches only and says the shift 'adds none'. I confirm that BEQ in_hazel (&9CFC) and BEQ gathered (&9EFD) stop crossing, and that no other branch in &98F8-&A319 changes or goes out of range. But the shift also moves data read through indexed and indirect reads, and those were not counted. (1) LDX ck_index,Y at &9CDE: ck_index moves from &A3B2 to &A3B4, so Y=&4C and &4D now cross a page as well as Y>=&4E. Measured 4.70 cycles an execution, so about 70% of reads already cross and Y is in that range; the +1s this adds were not counted. (2) LDY wa_rows_guess,X (&A0F5 to &A0F7): X=9 and 10 would now cross. The profile shows every execution already crossing (19.92/3.99=5.0), so this costs nothing measurable. (3) The straight sprites (straight_35..4a, &A530-&B3xx) all move 2 bytes. They are read in the hot byte loop by LDA (d_ptr),Y at &9C34 and &9C7A (about 64 executions a pass on seed 1, 80 holding RIGHT; 2.5% and 0.2% cross now). The page tests on col_ptr (BCC on_same_page, BCS empty_hi) and on d_ptr (BCS data_same_page) also change. Which drawn cells straddle a page changes with the data, so each straddling cell can gain or lose up to 2 cycles a draw. Nobody has measured the net effect, and it is the same size as the claimed 1.9 cycles a pass plus about 1 from the branches. The project rule 'no data moves' also touches sprite_column_count, ck_index, the ck_* tables and the straight sprites, which all move by 2. The saving a pass is not established, so I refute: rebuild and measure with passbench/pcprof before taking it.
